source.summary: GitHub Actions 'Embedder footprint' runs for the PR #384 Codex review fix (branch fix/365-eq-face-identity at head 3f7431ffe5c5ab1288d74a3a16f4b427f5f98797 — the remaining (eq) face consumers in typed bindings, annotated-name shape checks, canon resource ops, value types and value imports now resolve the face to the type it denotes before inspecting shape or kind) on top of the #365 change at dbcb675; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45825636440, 45825653204 and 45825670500 against the branch produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series; the branch was then merged with main cc6550bce007ca8d747160778aab6c3e41af272e (PR #381, the #193 register mapping), and the four core-jit series in this file are retained from PR #381's campaign (workflow_dispatch runs 45817815567, 45817829767 and 45817843974)
source.derivation: Re-baseline for the PR #384 Codex review fix (the remaining (eq) face consumers resolve the face to the type it denotes before inspecting shape or kind), following the #365 re-baseline at dbcb675. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45825689603, 45825709336 and 45825736689 on main at cc6550bce007ca8d747160778aab6c3e41af272e; all three runs pass the gate). This fix's own delta against the main control is confined to the three configurations that link telomere-component: in release, stripped file +6,432 B and stripped .text +6,048 B on all three; in release-size, stripped file +3,952 B (component) and +3,936 B (wasi, wasi-threads) and stripped .text +3,344 B (component) and +3,328 B (wasi, wasi-threads). Every other series is byte-identical to main in both profiles except core-jit, where the branch measures below both the main control and the checked-in baseline because main gained core-jit size after this branch's merge point. Against the checked-in baseline only the three release stripped file series grow (component +1,984 B, wasi +2,000 B, wasi-threads +2,000 B; every .text series and every release-size series measures at or below its retained baseline), so only those three series are re-baselined to the branch measurements and every other baseline is retained, following the established practice of re-baselining growth only. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release component stripped file series at +11.61% (2,433,656 B to 2,716,200 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison. Merge note for the integration with main cc6550bce007ca8d747160778aab6c3e41af272e (PR #381): the four core-jit series are retained from PR #381's second re-baseline campaign (branch runs 45817815567, 45817829767 and 45817843974; main control runs 45817858119, 45817871880 and 45817883664 on main at 2d653bfae0bd3ac995c17a0d26154f531762d28c), which re-baselined them for the #193 register mapping and the Codex P2 REX fix in movsx_vreg32; against the original #164 baseline those series stand at +8.32% (release stripped file, 1,989,584 B to 2,155,128 B), +7.48% (release stripped .text), +4.57% (release-size stripped file) and +4.24% (release-size stripped .text). The three release stripped file series of the component-linked configurations are from this PR's campaign above, and every other series is identical in the two campaigns' baselines, so the merged file is the union of the two re-baselines.
